name: Beefeater
label: Dischord
lede: Tomas Squip, a vegetarian who had drummed in Red C, fronted a band called Beefeater for two years and two LPs, while Fred Smith's guitar taught DC punk to swing.

eras.title: A Swiss drummer becomes the singer
eras.text: Tomas Squip came to Washington from Switzerland around 1981 and drummed in Red C before he ever sang. By 1984 he fronted a band built on Fred Smith's guitar and Dug Birdzell's bass, with a sound that owed as much to funk and jazz as to hardcore.

years.h: A Swiss drummer lands in DC and joins Red C
years.p: About nineteen and new from Switzerland, [[Tomas Squip|273702be-180d-487a-9238-2154aea60b92]] plays drums in Red C. He goes vegetarian within a year or so, a choice that ends up coloring the whole scene.

years.h: Beefeater forms around Squip's voice and Smith's guitar
years.p: Squip sings, Fred "Freak" Smith plays guitar, Dug E. Bird (Dug Birdzell) plays bass and Bruce Atchley Taylor drums.
years.xp: Smith was a Howard University music-education student whose father sang doo-wop. He also liked his guitars loud: NPR says he preferred the Scorpions and Michael Schenker to Led Zeppelin.

years.cap: Flier for a Beefeater show, September 29, 1984
years.h: Beefeater debuts at Food for Thought, funk and thrash in one set
years.p: The DC restaurant that hosts punk shows gets Beefeater's first gig. Funk, thrash and reggae share the set, with lyrics about politics and spirit.
years.xp:
Dischord's history dates the first show to the summer of 1984 and the band's active run to fall 1984 through fall 1986. The mix was the point: Fred Smith's guitar was aggressive but loose, and Dug Birdzell slapped his bass the way Smith had shown him.

Birdzell has credited Smith with teaching him slap bass. Listeners have heard the [[Minutemen|d4ad0149-d8ae-4105-8009-0221fce9ff35]] in that combination: punk energy pushed through funk and jazz.

eras.title: Revolution Summer
eras.text: DC hardcore had worn itself out on violence and the kids who came for it. In 1985 a handful of bands tried to make it mean something again, and Beefeater, with its politics and its groove, was one of them.

yt: Full set, Lake Braddock Community Center, 1985
years.h: Beefeater joins Revolution Summer with politics and a groove
years.p: The season also has [[Embrace|9d1ad8e3-8740-429a-bdc5-52f96a9c4431]], [[Gray Matter|c9065214-ba09-4c2c-b341-35713b702264]] and [[Rites of Spring|b2ff1a6d-9198-4646-b068-8965242d245b]]. [[Tomas Squip|273702be-180d-487a-9238-2154aea60b92]]'s lyrics are political and openly spiritual, unusual on Dischord.
years.xp: Dischord's own history says Beefeater's pointed approach, joined with Rites of Spring's intensity, became "the inspiration for much of the music that would come out of the Washington punk scene for years to come."

years.h: Plays for Lovers: Dischord No. 17, produced by "Gumbo MacKaye"
years.p: Recorded at Inner Ear, Beefeater's debut LP has A Dog Day, which follows a dog into a slaughterhouse.
years.xp:
[[Ian MacKaye|c12f644b-1066-4ead-b0dd-d0c380f5cca2]] was still calling A Dog Day a great song in 2023.

Squip's vegetarianism wasn't a side note. Soulside's Bobby Sullivan later credited him as the one who got his friends looking at the bigger picture, vegan diet included.

eras.title: Three drummers and one finished album
eras.text: Beefeater went through three drummers, put out an EP on another label, and broke up in the fall of 1986 with an album nobody had heard yet. Their roadie, Joe Lally, was about to join Fugazi.

years.cap: Flier for a Beefeater show with a photo collage, February 1, 1986
years.h: Bruce Taylor leaves, and Mark Shellhaas takes the sticks
years.p: Founding drummer Bruce Atchley Taylor is out. Mark Shellhaas plays on the Need a Job EP.

years.h: Need a Job goes out on Olive Tree, not Dischord
years.p: Six songs, and the only Beefeater record on another label.
years.xp: Wikipedia lists the EP as Olive Tree Records catalog No. 106.

years.h: Kenny Craun, drummer number three, plays House Burning Down
years.p: Third Beefeater drummer in two years.

years.h: Joe Lally hauls Beefeater's gear and lands in Fugazi
years.p: [[Joe Lally|62046ffd-7d76-476b-bee5-b281b7575c6c]] roadies for Beefeater and meets [[Ian MacKaye|c12f644b-1066-4ead-b0dd-d0c380f5cca2]], Squip's roommate. By late summer 1986 Lally is practicing with MacKaye in what becomes [[Fugazi|233fc3f3-6de2-465c-985e-e721dbabbace]].

yt: Full set, Chevy Chase Community Center, 1986
years.h: Beefeater quits with an album nobody has heard
years.p: Two years after the first show, the band is done. House Burning Down is recorded and still unreleased.

years.h: Full set at Chevy Chase Community Center, 1986
yt: Full set at Chevy Chase Community Center, 1986

years.h: After the breakup, House Burning Down, Dischord No. 23
years.p: Squip, Smith, Birdzell and Craun cut it at Inner Ear, again with MacKaye producing, with world music threaded through the funk.

eras.title: Everybody goes to another band
eras.text: The members scattered into other DC bands, Squip put what he believed into Dischord's own book, and the label packed both albums onto a single CD.

years.p: The pair play in Fidelity Jones until spring 1990. Smith joins the goth-leaning [[Strange Boutique|0ee0668b-fa1d-4db1-ac8c-43a3ad1272c0]], Craun the Rhythm Pigs.

years.h: Squip puts his beliefs in print in Threat by Example
years.p: His essay in the Dischord book lays out a plainly religious worldview, rare among Dischord voices. He later records a solo album, My Happiness, and renames himself Onam Ben-Israel, then Onam Emmet.

years.h: Both albums share one CD, Dischord No. 64
years.p: Plays for Lovers and House Burning Down, with bonus tracks: the whole Dischord run of Beefeater in one place.

eras.title: Onam Emmet and Freak
eras.text: Squip went looking for God and found more than one path. Fred Smith kept playing, from post-punk to what he called ghetto metal, took FREAK as his legal name, and was killed in Los Angeles in 2017. NPR reported that December that no one had been named.

years.big: "We were kind of the band that made it all right to talk about vegetarianism."
years.h: Squip, now Onam Emmet, sums up what the band did
years.p: Squip, in a 2010 interview. He also says he spent sixteen years in the African Hebrew Israelite community, a vegan group, before embracing the Sikh path.
years.xp: Washington City Paper had earlier covered his months at the community's commune in Israel.

years.h: Fred Smith plays his last DC show at the Black Cat
years.p: By then the Beefeater guitarist has also played in Strange Boutique, American Corpse Flower and Blaxmyth.

q: His guitar playing was such a strong element.
years.h: Fred Smith is found stabbed in a San Fernando park
years.p: NPR reported that Smith, homeless and in his mid-fifties, was found dead in Las Palmas Park.
years.xp:
Smith had recently left Blake House, a sober-living facility, and was sleeping on buses and showering at the YMCA, NPR reported.

MacKaye told NPR he'd noticed manic emails and that Smith was dealing with issues of his own. Dug Birdzell credited Smith with the band's funk, down to teaching him how to slap.

Police treated the death as a homicide. In December 2017 Los Angeles County offered a $10,000 reward, and Supervisor Sheila Kuehl said Smith "paved the way for African-American musicians in the punk genre." No one had been named.
